a: To give the board enough information to decide whether to authorize the next stage.

What does an end stage report cover?

q: The beta is complete. Can Zosia authorize the next management stage herself?
a: No; the project board authorizes it. The board decides whether to commit funds to the next stage.

q: Which report summarizes the stage that has just finished?
a: End stage report. It gives the board evidence of performance against the stage plan.

q: What must Zosia update when forecast maintenance costs increase?
a: Business case and relevant forecasts. Continued business justification may be affected.

q: Who prepares the next stage plan at a stage boundary?
a: Project manager. The project manager prepares a detailed plan for board approval.

q: Who authorizes the start of the next stage?
a: Project board. It reviews the stage end information and decides.

q: Which report evaluates the beta against its approved stage plan?
a: End stage report. It compares performance with the authorized plan.

q: Why update the business case after changes to API costs?
a: To test continued business justification. The project should remain desirable, viable and achievable.

q: Which plan updates the view of the entire investment?
a: Project plan. The project plan gives an overall view across management stages.

q: The board requests a replacement plan for an exception. What does Zosia prepare?
a: Exception plan for authorization. It is prepared in response to a board decision on an exception.

q: How does an exception plan differ from an exception report?
a: The plan proposes replacement delivery; the report explains a forecast exception. One proposes a route forward, the other supplies the escalation.

q: What does Maya contribute to the stage boundary assessment?
a: User test results and evidence of product fitness. The senior user represents user expectations and benefits.
